title: A comprehensive atlas of the bonobo gut bacteriome and its associated host and exposome factors.
ehr_evidence: Data were collected using observations, historical records retrieved from the studbook or from the Zoological Information Management System (ZIMS), questionnaires and diet sheets filled in by zoo staff.
summary: Comprehensive atlas of the bonobo gut bacteriome and its associated host and exposome factors, comparing wild and zoo-housed populations to identify drivers of microbiome composition and social transmission.
key_findings: Gut bacterial beta diversity was significantly associated with captive vs wild lifestyle (PERMANOVA: R2 = 28.7%, p < 0.001).
Wild bonobo alpha diversity was higher than zoo-housed bonobos (LMM: β = 0.935 ± 0.311 SE, p = 0.020).
Dietary diversity was negatively correlated with alpha diversity in wild bonobos (LMM: β = −0.353 ± 0.077 SE, padj < 0.001).
Antibiotic use was associated with lower similarity to the wild phenotype (posterior mean = −0.298, 95% CI: [−0.407, −0.189]).
Current cohabitation led to the highest gut bacteria sharing (36.5% Bray-Curtis similarity on average), followed by past cohabitation (30.1% similarity).
Grooming bond strength strongly correlated with gut bacteriome similarity (posterior mean = 1.055, 95% CI: [0.496, 1.609]).
study_design: Cross-sectional observational study with dyadic analyses comparing wild and zoo-housed bonobos
data_source_type: Fecal microbiome sequencing and field/zoo observational data
population: 212 bonobos (Pan paniscus) from European zoos and two wild communities in the Democratic Republic of the Congo
exposure_domain: Diet, antibiotic use, social contact, cohabitation, age, maternal effects, and environmental conditions
limitations: Assumes wild bonobo bacteriome represents a native baseline
Relies on 16S rRNA sequencing rather than metagenomics, limiting strain-level resolution
Dietary intake estimated from group distribution rather than individual consumption
Cross-sectional design limits causal inference for social transmission
data_availability_statement: Sequencing data have been deposited at the European Nucleotide Archive under project ENA: PRJEB86099 and are publicly available as of the date of publication. Pseudonymized sample data have been deposited and are publicly available as of the data of publication at Zenodo: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.14913431. All original code has been deposited and is publicly available as of the date of publication at Zenodo: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.14911049.
